Rashi on Eruvin 98b:10:1.hebrew: משתמש בכל הכותל - אם הזיז מוטל לארכו אצל הכותל על פני כולו, משתמש בכל הזיז:
Rashi on Eruvin 98b:10:1.english: One may use along the entire wall - If the ledge lies along its length alongside the wall across all of it, one may use the entire ledge:

Rashi on Eruvin 98b:10:2.hebrew: עד עשרה התחתונים - כלומר, כל מקום שהוא — בין סמוך לחלון מיד, בין מופלג הימנו הרבה — ובלבד שלא יהא בתוך עשרה תחתונים שברשות הרבים:
Rashi on Eruvin 98b:10:2.english: Until the lower ten [handbreadths] - That is to say, wherever it is — whether immediately adjacent to the window or far removed from it — provided that it is not within the lower ten [handbreadths], which are in the public domain.

Rashi on Eruvin 98b:10:3.english: Below it - [Yet] above ten [handbreadths from the ground].

Rashi on Eruvin 98b:10:4.hebrew: משתמש בו - בתחתון, ע"פ כל הכותל, אם מונח לאורכו אצל הכותל:
Rashi on Eruvin 98b:10:4.english: One may use it - [He may use] the lower [ledge], along the entire wall, if it is placed along its length next to the wall.

Rashi on Eruvin 98b:11:1.english: This ledge - [This refers to the] upper [ledge: the Gemara asks,] what are the circumstances?

Rashi on Eruvin 98b:11:2.hebrew: אי דלית ביה ארבעה מקום פטור הוא - ואפילו כנגד חלונו לא לשתמש — נהי דמקום פטור הוא ומותר לכתף עליו, כדקי"ל: מקום שאין בו ארבעה מותר לבני רה"ר ולבני רה"י לכתף עליו — מיהו תשמיש תדיר לא משתרי ביה, דלא חזי לתשמישתא, ושכיחי כלים למיפל לרה"ר. ואע"ג דאוקמינן בכלים הנשברים, הני מילי בדאית ביה ד', דלא שכיחי למיפל כולי האי; אבל הכא דרובא נפלי, מחזי כמאן דשדי להדיא לרשות הרבים:
Rashi on Eruvin 98b:11:2.english: If it does not have four, it is an exempt domain - And [as for the Gemara's objection,] “even opposite his window he should not use [it]” — although it is an exempt domain and it is permitted to adjust loads upon it, as we maintain: “A place that does not have four [handbreadths], it is permitted for people of the public domain and people of the private domain to adjust loads upon it,” nevertheless, regular use is not permitted on it, as it is not suitable for use and utensils are likely to fall into the public domain. And even though we established [the Mishnah as referring] to breakable vessels, that applies [only] when it has four [handbreadths], where they are not all that likely to fall; but here, where most [vessels] fall, it appears like one who throws [them] directly into the public domain.

Rashi on Eruvin 98b:12:1.hebrew: חורי חלון הוא - כלומר, זוית החלון והרחבתו הוא. ולשון חורי דנקט — משום דגבי שבת שייך למימר: חורי רשות הרבים כרשות הרבים, וכן חורי רה"י כרה"י דמי; כגון כותל הסמוכה לרה"ר ויש בה חורין פתוחין לרה"ר, למטה מיו"ד — הוי רה"ר:
Rashi on Eruvin 98b:12:1.english: It is the recesses of the window - That is to say, it is the corner of the window and its widening. And as for the phrasing of "recesses" that [Abaye] used, [it is] because with regard to Shabbat it is applicable to say: "The recesses of the public domain [are] like the public domain, and similarly the recesses of a private domain are considered like a private domain"; for example, a wall adjacent to the public domain that has holes opening into the public domain — [if they are] below ten [handbreadths], it is [considered] the public domain.

Rashi on Eruvin 98b:13:1.hebrew: עומד אדם ברה"י - בבית או על הגג, ושוחה ונוטל חפץ ברה"ר כאן ומניחו כאן:
Rashi on Eruvin 98b:13:1.english: A person may stand in a private domain - In a house or on a roof, and bend down and take an object in the public domain here and place it there.

Rashi on Eruvin 98b:13:2.hebrew: ובלבד שלא יוציאנו מארבע אמותיו - ממקום שהיה מונח בו. ואשמועי' מתניתין דלא גזרינן שמא יכניסנו אצלו:
Rashi on Eruvin 98b:13:2.english: Provided that he does not carry it beyond its four cubits - From the place where it was resting. And our Mishnah teaches us that we do not decree lest he bring it in to himself.

Rashi on Eruvin 98b:14:1.hebrew: וישתין ברה"ר - דמפיק מרה"י לרה"ר:
Rashi on Eruvin 98b:14:1.english: And urinate into a public domain - For he takes [it] out from a private domain to a public domain.

Rashi on Eruvin 98b:15:1.english: Once his spittle has detached in his mouth - From [the time] it has become repulsive and gathered to come out.

Rashi on Eruvin 98b:15:2.hebrew: לא יהלך ארבע אמות עד שירוק - דכיון דלמשדייא קאי, משאוי הוא:
Rashi on Eruvin 98b:15:2.english: He may not walk four cubits until he spits - For since it stands to be cast out, it is a burden.

Rashi on Eruvin 98b:16:1.english: Rav taught him, etc. - [This is a] decree lest he bring it in to himself.

Rashi on Eruvin 98b:16:2.hebrew: ועבדת כר"מ - דאיהו הוא דגזר שמא יביא אצלו, כדלקמן בפירקין [עירובין דף קא.]: לא יעמוד ברשות היחיד ויפתח ברשות הרבים — שיטול מפתח ברשות הרבים ויפתח בו פתח הסמוך לרשות הרבים — שמא יכניס אצלו במקום שהוא:
Rashi on Eruvin 98b:16:2.english: And you acted in accordance with Rabbi Meir - For it is he who decreed lest one bring [the object] to oneself, as [stated] later in our chapter [Eruvin 101a]: "A person may not stand in a private domain and open [a door] in a public domain" — that he takes a key in the public domain and opens with it a door adjacent to the public domain — lest he bring [it] in to himself, into the place where he is.

Rashi on Eruvin 98b:1:1.hebrew: למטה משלשה - הגיע ראש הספר לשלשה סמוך לקרקע — ארעא סמיכתא הוא, והרי הוא כמונח:
Rashi on Eruvin 98b:1:1.english: Below three [handbreadths] - [If] the end of the scroll reached within three [handbreadths] close to the ground — it is [considered] solid ground, and it is [therefore] as [though it were] resting [on the ground].

Rashi on Eruvin 98b:3:1.hebrew: אלא הא דאמר רבא - בפ' הזורק במס' שבת (דף ק.):
Rashi on Eruvin 98b:3:1.english: Rather, that which Rava said - This is stated in chapter HaZorek, in Tractate Shabbat (daf 100a).

Rashi on Eruvin 98b:3:2.hebrew: תוך שלשה לרבנן - דפליגי עליה דר"ע בקלוטה כמי שהונחה, ואמרי: דהזורק מרשות היחיד לרשות היחיד דרך רשות הרבים למטה מעשרה, לא אמרינן "הואיל ונקלטה ביו"ד תחתונים שהן רה"ר, הרי היא כמי שהונחה" לחייבו — אפי' זרק למטה משלשה לא מיחייב, אם עד שלא הגיע לארץ נשרף או בלעו כלב, אלא אם כן נח על גבי משהו; ואפילו לא הוי מקום ארבעה, הויא הנחה. ולמעלה משלשה, אם נח — פטור, ואפי' לר"ע; דאי מקום ארבעה הוא — כרמלית הוא, ואי לית ביה ארבעה — מקום פטור הוא:
Rashi on Eruvin 98b:3:2.english: Within three [handbreadths], according to the Rabbis - Who disagree with Rabbi Akiva regarding [the principle that an object] caught [in the air is] as if it has rested, and they say that [in the case of] one who throws [an object] from a private domain to a private domain via a public domain below ten [handbreadths], we do not say, "Since it was caught in the lower ten [handbreadths], which are a public domain, it is as if it has rested," so as to make him liable. [Rava teaches that] even if he threw [it] below three [handbreadths], he is not liable if, before it reached the ground, it was burned or a dog swallowed it, unless it rested on something; and even if it is not an area of four [by four handbreadths], it is [considered] a resting. And above three [handbreadths], if it rested, he is exempt, and even according to Rabbi Akiva; for if it is an area of four [handbreadths], it is a *karmelit*, and if it does not have four [handbreadths] in it, it is an exempt domain.

Rashi on Eruvin 98b:3:3.hebrew: נימא כתנאי אמרה לשמעתיה - דהא תנא קמא, אפילו כי לא נח נמי, גזר למטה מג', משום דילמא זמנין דאין אגדו בידו. ולרבא, כי אין אגדו בידו נמי, כי האי גוונא דלא נח — לא מיחייב, אם קלטו והחזירו קודם שנח:
Rashi on Eruvin 98b:3:3.english: Shall we say he stated his teaching in accordance with Tannaim? - For the first tanna, even when it did not come to rest, decreed [against rolling it back] below three [handbreadths], lest sometimes its binding not be in his hand. But according to Rava, even when its binding is not in his hand, in a case like this where it did not come to rest, he is not liable if he caught it and brought it back before it came to rest.

Rashi on Eruvin 98b:6:1.hebrew: זיז שלפני החלון - בולט מן הכותל, גבוה י' ורחב ד':
Rashi on Eruvin 98b:6:1.english: A ledge in front of the window - Protruding from the wall, ten [handbreadths] high and four [handbreadths] wide.

Rashi on Eruvin 98b:6:2.hebrew: נותנין עליו - בני עלייה, דרה"י הוא:
Rashi on Eruvin 98b:6:2.english: One may place [objects] upon it - The residents of the upper story [may do so], for it is a private domain.

Rashi on Eruvin 98b:7:1.english: That protrudes to where - To where does it protrude?

Rashi on Eruvin 98b:7:2.english: That it protrudes into a private domain - Into a courtyard.

Rashi on Eruvin 98b:8:1.hebrew: כלים הנשברים - כלי חרס וזכוכית, שאם נפלו ישברו, דליכא למימר דילמא אזיל ומייתי להו:
Rashi on Eruvin 98b:8:1.english: Fragile utensils - Earthenware and glass vessels, which, if they fall, will break, so that one cannot say, "Perhaps he will go and bring them [back]."

Rashi on Eruvin 98b:9:1.hebrew: קערות וכוסות וקיתוניות - כולם כלים הנשברים הם, דסתמייהו דחרס:
Rashi on Eruvin 98b:9:1.english: Bowls, and cups, and jugs - They are all breakable utensils, as they are typically [made] of earthenware.

Tosafot on Eruvin 98b:10:1.hebrew: ומשתמש בכל הכותל עד עשרה תחתונים - פי' בקונטרס: אם הזיז מוטל לארכו על פני כל הכותל, משתמש בכל הזיז. וקשה לר"י, דהיינו סיפא, דקתני: "אם יש זיז למטה הימנו משתמש בו". ומפרש ר"י, דבחורין שבכותל קאמר דמשתמש; ולשון "משתמש בכל הכותל" משמע נמי כן:
Tosafot on Eruvin 98b:10:1.english: "And one may use the entire wall until the lower ten [handbreadths]" - Rashi explained: If the ledge extends along its length across the entire wall, one may use the entire ledge. And the Ri finds this difficult, for this is the seifa, which teaches: "If there is a ledge below it, one may use it." And the Ri explains that it means one may use the holes in the wall; and the phrasing "one may use the entire wall" also implies this.

Tosafot on Eruvin 98b:11:1.hebrew: אי דלית ליה ארבע אפי' כנגד חלונו נמי לא ישתמש - משמע מפירוש הקונט', דברחב ד' משתמש בכלים הנשברים, אבל שאין רחב — לא ישתמש אפי' כלים הנשברים, דהוי כאילו שדי להו להדיא. וקשה לר"י: דכיון דאפילו ברחב ד' לא ישתמש בכלים שאין נשברין, א"כ אפילו רחב מאה אמה נמי! דלענין שבת חשיב רחב ד' כרחב אלף. ונראה לר"י, דברחב ד' שרי ליתן אפילו כלים שאינן נשברים, ומתני' — ברחב כל שהוא. והא דלא מוקי לה ברחב ד' ובכל כלים — משום דסתם זיז אינו רחב ד'. וכי פריך הש"ס: "אי דלית ביה ארבעה, אפילו כנגד חלונו לא ישתמש" — ה"מ למיפרך: אפי' בשלמטה הימנו לא ישתמש! והא דלא משני ליה דבכלים הנשברים איירי — היינו משום דלא מיתוקמא בהכי ע"כ, מדלא שרי בשאר הכותל אלא כנגד חלונו בלבד:
Tosafot on Eruvin 98b:11:1.english: "If it does not have four, even opposite his window he should also not use [it]" - It is implied from the commentary of Rashi [ha-Kuntres] that on [a ledge that is] four [handbreadths] wide, one may use [it for] fragile utensils, but [on a ledge] that is not [four handbreadths] wide, one may not use [it] even [for] fragile utensils, as it is as though he throws them directly [into the public domain]. And the Ri questions [this]: Since even on [a ledge that is] four [handbreadths] wide one may not use [it for] utensils that are not fragile, if so, even [if it were] one hundred cubits wide [it should] also [be forbidden], because with regard to Shabbat, four [handbreadths] wide is considered like a thousand wide! And it appears to the Ri that on [a ledge that is] four [handbreadths] wide, it is permitted to place even utensils that are not fragile, and our Mishnah is [dealing with a ledge of] any width whatever. And that which [the Gemara] does not establish it [as dealing with a ledge that is] four [handbreadths] wide and with all utensils — [that is] because an ordinary ledge is not four [handbreadths] wide. And when the Gemara asks: "If it does not have four [handbreadths], even opposite his window he should also not use [it]," it could have objected: Even on the [ledge] below it he should not use [it]! And that which [the Gemara] does not answer that it is dealing with fragile utensils — that is because it perforce cannot be established in that manner, since [the baraita] does not permit [usage] along the rest of the wall, but only opposite his window alone.

Tosafot on Eruvin 98b:12:1.hebrew: תחתון דאית ביה ד' - ק"ק: דמעליון שמעינן ליה דשרינן כנגד חלונו משום דחלון משלימתו לד'? ויש לומר: דאיצטריך לאשמועינן בתחתון, אף על גב דלא ניחא תשמישתא — דהא איכא עליון דמפסיק:
Tosafot on Eruvin 98b:12:1.english: “The lower [ledge] that has four” - It is somewhat difficult: For from [the ruling regarding] the upper [ledge] we learn that we permit [use] opposite his window because the window completes it to four [handbreadths; why, then, did the baraita need to mention the lower ledge]? And one can say that it was necessary [for the baraita] to teach us regarding the lower [ledge, that one may use it] even though its use is not convenient, as there is the upper [ledge] that intervenes [between the window and it].

Tosafot on Eruvin 98b:3:1.hebrew: נימא כתנאי אמרה לשמעתיה - אע"ג דלא ניחא הכא לאוקמי מילתא דרבא בפלוגתא דתנאי דמתני', מ"מ ע"כ אשכחן ברייתא דפליגא עליה במסכת שבת בפ' הזורק (שבת דף צז.), גבי הזורק מרה"י לרה"י ורה"ר באמצע, דקתני בברייתא: תוך ג' ד"ה חייב. אי נמי, יש לחלק: דהכא שבא החפץ מלמעלה מג' למטה לתוך ג' — הוא דבעי רבא הנחה על גבי משהו; אבל התם איירי שהיה החפץ תוך ג' משיצא מתחת ידו, להכי חשיב כמונח, דהא מודה רבא דהמעביר בתוך שלשה דכמונח בקרקע דמי, כדמוכח בפרק המוציא יין (שבת דף פ.). והא דלא חשבינן מתגלגל כמונח בסוף הזורק (שבת דף ק.) — התם איירי כשהיתה תחילת זריקה למעלה מג':
Tosafot on Eruvin 98b:3:1.english: Let us say that he stated his halakha in accordance with the tanna’im - Even though [the Gemara] here is reluctant to establish Rava’s statement as [dependent on] the dispute of the tanna’im of the Mishnah, nevertheless, perforce we find a baraita that disagrees with him in tractate Shabbat in the chapter [entitled] Hazorek (Shabbat 97a), regarding one who throws from a private domain to a private domain with a public domain in between, as it is taught in a baraita: [If the object travels] within three [handbreadths of the ground], all agree that he is liable. Alternatively, one can differentiate: here, where the object came from above three [handbreadths] down into [the airspace of] within three [handbreadths], that is where Rava requires resting upon something; but there, it is dealing with [a case where] the object was within three [handbreadths] from the time it left his hand. Therefore, it is considered as [if it were] at rest, for Rava concedes that one who carries [an object] within three [handbreadths of the ground] is considered as if it is resting on the ground, as is proven in the chapter [entitled] Hamotzi Yayin (Shabbat 80a). And as for that which we do not consider a rolling [object] as at rest at the end of Hazorek (Shabbat 100a) — there it is dealing with [a case where] the beginning of the throw was above three [handbreadths].

Tosafot on Eruvin 98b:4:1.hebrew: אלא כולה רבי יהודה היא - תימה, דבשבת בפרק הזורק (שבת דף צז:) בעי למימר דסבר ר' יהודה: "קלוטה כמו שהונחה", גבי הזורק מרה"י לרה"ר, ועבר ד' אמות ברה"ר. ולמסקנא דהתם ניחא, דמוקי לה כגון דאמר: "כדנפקא לרה"ר תנוח", דמסתבר טפי למימר התם: "קלוטה כמו שהונחה", כיון שהיה דעתו ורצונו שתנוח שם; אבל הכא, דאין רצונו שיפול שם הספר, אין לנו לומר שיהא כמונח. אבל למאי דס"ד התם מעיקרא דמיחייב שתים, ובאומר "כל מקום שתרצה שם תנוח" — קשה. ויש לחלק, דהתם אינו מקפיד על החפץ אנה שינוח, אבל הכא מקפיד, ומרצונו היה חפץ שלא היה שם מונח. אבל לרבא קשיא, דאפי' באומר "כל מקום שתרצה תנוח" בעי רבא הנחה על גבי משהו; דמקפיד — אפילו נח על גבי משהו לא מיחייב, דלא נעשית מחשבתו. וצריך לומר, דלמאי דס"ד התם מעיקרא, לית ליה דרבא. ועוד יש לומר, כדפרישית לעיל, דהתם כשתחילת זריקתו תוך שלשה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 98b:4:1.english: "Rather, it is all Rabbi Yehuda" - It is astonishing, for in Shabbat in the chapter entitled Hazorek (Shabbat 97b), the Gemara wanted to say that Rabbi Yehuda holds that an object intercepted in airspace is as if it has come to rest, regarding one who throws an object from the private domain into the public domain and it traveled four cubits in the public domain. And according to the conclusion there it is well, for the Gemara establishes it in a case such as where he said, "When it exits into the public domain, let it rest," as it is more reasonable to say there that "intercepted is as if it has come to rest," since it was his intention and desire that it rest there; but here, where it is not his desire that the scroll fall there, we should not say that it is considered at rest. But according to what originally entered our minds there at first, that he is liable for two sin-offerings, and it is where he says, "Any place that it wants, let it rest there" — it is difficult. And one can distinguish: there he is not particular about the object as to where it rests, but here he is particular, and of his will he desired that it would not be resting there. But according to Rava it is difficult, for even where he says, "Any place that it wants, let it rest," Rava requires coming to rest upon something tangible; and here, since he is particular, even if it rested upon something tangible he would not be liable, as his intention was not fulfilled. And one must say that according to what originally entered our minds there at first, the Gemara does not accept Rava's view. And furthermore, one can say, as I explained above, that there it is a case where the beginning of his throw was within three handbreadths of the ground.

Tosafot on Eruvin 98b:7:1.hebrew: ניחוש דילמא נפיל ואתי לאיתויי - ואי דמפיק לכרמלית או לחצר שאינה מעורבת: לרבא, דלית ליה לקמן (עירובין צט.) גזירה לגזירה, פשיטא דשרי, דלא איצטריך למיתני; ולאביי, דגזר — אסור, כמו במפיק לרה"ר. ועוד נראה, מדמשני אביי "לעולם דמפיק לרה"ר", משמע דבמפיק לכרמלית או לחצר שאינה מעורבת שרי, אפילו כלים שאינן נשברים. ואע"ג דלקמן גזר אביי גזירה לגזירה, יש לחלק, כמו שפירשתי לעיל. ובפרק כיצד משתתפין (לעיל עירובין דף פד.), גבי אנשי חצר ואנשי עלייה ששכחו ולא עירבו, דקתני: "זיז היוצא מן הכותל", בעשרה דעלייה הוי לעלייה — אפילו הניח שם כלים שאינם נשברים:
Tosafot on Eruvin 98b:7:1.english: "We should be concerned lest it fall and he will come to bring it" - And if [the Gemara had suggested] that it protrudes into a karmelit or into a courtyard that was not joined [by an eiruv]: According to Rava, who does not accept [decreeing] a decree upon a decree later (Eruvin 99a), it is obvious that it is permitted, such that it did not need to be taught; and according to Abaye, who does decree [a decree upon a decree], it is prohibited, just as when it protrudes into a public domain. Furthermore, it appears [to be so], since Abaye answers, "Actually, [it is a case] where it protrudes into a public domain," which implies that where it protrudes into a karmelit or into a courtyard that was not joined, it is permitted even [for] utensils that do not break. And even though later Abaye decrees a decree upon a decree, one can distinguish [between the cases], as I explained above. And [it is likewise evident] in the chapter [entitled] Keitzad Mishtatfin (above, Eruvin 84a) regarding the residents of a courtyard and the residents of an upper story who forgot and did not establish an eiruv, where it teaches: "[If] a ledge protrudes from the wall," within the [upper] ten [handbreadths] of the upper story it belongs to the upper story — [meaning] even to place there utensils that do not break.
